title: Precise vanishing for maps from a truncated bounded projective complex
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of projective objects with $P^i=0$ for $i<n$, and let $K^\bullet$ be a complex such that $H^i(K^\bullet)=0$ for every $i\ge n$. Then every morphism from $Q(P^\bullet)$ to $Q(K^\bullet)$ in the derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is zero, where $Q$ is the localization functor at quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: The vanishing homology hypothesis gives K.IsLE (n-1), so the canonical inclusion K.truncLE (n-1) → K is a quasi-isomorphism, by Mathlib CochainComplex.quasiIso_ιTruncLE_iff. Its image under Q is an isomorphism. This is the canonical lower-truncation reduction of Tag 064D, with the acyclic complementary term eliminated directly by localization.

Apply [lem-pc-ring-precise-vanishing-core] to P and K.truncLE (n-1). Represent every homotopy morphism by a chain map using fullness of the quotient. Each component is zero: for i<n its source P.X i is zero; for i≥n its target (K.truncLE (n-1)).X i is zero. Thus all derived maps to this lower truncation vanish.
For f : Q(P) → Q(K), compose with the inverse of Q applied to the truncation inclusion. Step 2 makes this composite zero. Postcompose with the inclusion isomorphism to conclude f=0.
